subChunks.title: Junior Capstone — Dashboard Layout
subChunks.hookHtml: You've covered grid layouts, responsive design, state variants, dark mode, transitions, component extraction, forms, tables, badges, navigation patterns, modals, sidebars, lists, skeleton loaders, alerts, media handling, scroll behaviour, container queries, and print styles. Now compose them into the component that uses all of them: an admin dashboard.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Dashboard anatomy

A production dashboard has five distinct regions, each built from the utilities you've learned:

/* 1. App shell: grid sidebar + main */
<div class="grid grid-cols-[240px_1fr] min-h-screen">
  <aside class="flex flex-col h-screen sticky top-0 border-r border-gray-200">

/* 2. Sticky inner header (inside main) */
  <main class="flex flex-col min-h-screen">
    <header class="sticky top-0 z-10 bg-white/90 backdrop-blur-md border-b border-gray-100 px-8 py-4">

/* 3. Stats row */
    <div class="grid grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4">
      <!-- stat cards -->

/* 4. Content grid (table + activity feed) */
    <div class="grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-[1fr_320px] gap-6">

/* 5. Notification toast (fixed) */
<div class="fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-50">

Stat card pattern

<div class="bg-white rounded-xl p-6 border border-gray-100 shadow-sm
            hover:shadow-md transition">
  <div class="flex items-center justify-between">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-gray-500">Total XP</p>
    <div class="w-9 h-9 bg-blue-100 rounded-lg flex items-center justify-center">
      <span class="text-blue-600 text-lg">⚡</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="text-3xl font-bold text-gray-900 mt-3">48,291</p>
  <p class="text-sm text-emerald-600 mt-1 flex items-center gap-1">
    ↑ 12% from last month
  </p>
</div>

Connecting the regions

The quality of a dashboard comes from the connections between regions, not the individual components:

  • The sidebar active state and the header page title should agree
  • The stat cards and the data table should reference the same dataset
  • The activity feed and the table rows should be visually consistent
  • The empty state should appear when table rows are zero
  • The toast should appear after a table action

Lyra: "A dashboard is not a collection of components. It is a system. The sidebar knows where you are. The header names the page. The stats summarise the data. The table details it. The feed shows what changed. The toast confirms your actions. Build each region to reinforce the others, and the dashboard becomes a tool rather than a collection of boxes."

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Every component you have built in the Junior tier serves a purpose in the dashboard. The sidebar is your navigation system. The table is your data layer. The feed is your temporal layer. The stat cards are your summary layer. The toast is your action confirmation. Compose them deliberately, and the result is not a collection of boxes — it is an instrument.

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a complete analytics dashboard from scratch with no starter code. Requirements: a sidebar with navigation (active state on 'Analytics'), a frosted glass header with page title and date range selector, a 4-stat card row with responsive grid, a large data table with striped rows, hover states, badges, and an action column, an activity feed column beside the table, a skeleton loading state for one of the stat cards, an empty state in the table, and a toast notification in the bottom-right corner. Use dark mode variants on at least the sidebar and header.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Walk through the complete dashboard you just built, region by region. For each region: (1) what layout pattern does it use and why, (2) which Junior-tier concepts does it demonstrate, (3) what would break if you removed the key utility from each region? Identify the three most important class utilities in the entire dashboard — the ones whose absence would cause the most visible degradation.

questions.prompt: The dashboard header uses sticky top-0 z-10 bg-white/90 backdrop-blur-md. When the user scrolls, the main content table header (inside the table wrapper) also uses sticky top-0. The table header appears above the dashboard header. What z-index fix is needed?
options: The dashboard header needs a higher z-index (e.g. z-30) than the table header (z-10 or lower) — higher z-index wins when elements overlap
The table header should use position:absolute instead of sticky
Add overflow-hidden to the content area to prevent the table header from stacking
The table header shouldn't use sticky — use position:relative instead
questions.answer: The dashboard header needs a higher z-index (e.g. z-30) than the table header (z-10 or lower) — higher z-index wins when elements overlap
questions.explanation: When sticky elements overlap, z-index determines which is on top. The dashboard header should have a higher z-index (z-30) than any sticky element inside the main content area (z-10). This prevents table headers from appearing above the page navigation header. Consistent z-index layering is one of the most common issues in complex dashboard layouts.

questions.prompt: The content grid uses grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-[1fr_300px]. On a 900px screen (between md and lg), both the table and activity feed stack in a single column. A designer wants the feed to appear below the table on medium screens, not beside it. Is the current implementation correct for this requirement?
options: Yes — grid-cols-1 applies below lg breakpoint, so both stack on a 900px screen. The feed appears below the table (second in DOM order)
No — grid-cols-1 puts the feed to the right on all sizes, not below
No — CSS grid always places items side-by-side, never stacked
No — the 1fr column will always take full width, hiding the 300px feed column
questions.answer: Yes — grid-cols-1 applies below lg breakpoint, so both stack on a 900px screen. The feed appears below the table (second in DOM order)
questions.explanation: grid-cols-1 creates a single column grid where all children stack vertically in DOM order. At lg (≥1024px), grid-cols-[1fr_300px] creates the two-column layout with the table on the left and feed on the right. At 900px (below lg), the single-column layout means the table appears first (DOM order: first child) and the feed below it. The implementation is correct.

questions.prompt: A junior developer on your team adds overflow-hidden to the main content area to prevent a horizontal scrollbar caused by a wide data table. The table becomes unscrollable and data is cut off. What is the correct fix?
options: Wrap the table in its own overflow-x-auto div — this creates a horizontal scroll container for just the table, without affecting the main content area
Add min-w-0 to the main content area to prevent overflow
Keep overflow-hidden on main, but add overflow-visible on the table
Use overflow-scroll on the main area instead of overflow-hidden
questions.answer: Wrap the table in its own overflow-x-auto div — this creates a horizontal scroll container for just the table, without affecting the main content area
questions.explanation: overflow-hidden on the main area clips all child content — including the table — making it inaccessible. The correct fix is to contain the horizontal overflow at the table level: wrap the table in a div with overflow-x-auto. This creates a scrollable container for the table specifically, allowing users to scroll horizontally to see all columns, without affecting other content on the page.
